docs.title: LongGuard 🛡️
docs.text: The Chain-of-Thought Circuit Breaker for LangGraph and LangChain Agents.

docs.title: What is LongGuard?
docs.text:
LongGuard is a lightweight runtime safety net for autonomous LLM agents.

When agents encounter ambiguous tool outputs or unexpected failures, they often get stuck: - Calling the exact same tool with the exact same inputs 25 times in a row. - Cycling between two reasoning steps in an infinite loop. - Pursuing a dead-end direction that burns 30,000+ tokens.

Frameworks like LangGraph have a built-in recursion_limit, but it is a hard crash: it burns tokens until the limit, crashes with an unhandled GraphRecursionError, and loses the conversation state.

LongGuard catches loops early (typically within 4 steps), injects a "Reflect & Pivot" prompt to help the agent course-correct, and only kills the run gracefully if recovery fails.

CLOSED ──(loop detected)──▶ REFLECTING ──(persists)──▶ HALF_OPEN ──▶ OPEN (Kill)
   ▲                             │                         │
   └──────────(clean step)───────┴─────────────────────────┘

docs.text: What Happens Without LongGuard What Happens With LongGuard Agent repeats same tool 25 times Trapped at step 4 Crashes with unhandled 500 error Graceful exit with AI apology message Burns 40k+ tokens ($2.00–$5.00+ / query) Hard spend cap & early intervention Agent never knows why it failed Injected Reflect & Pivot prompt forces recovery Zero post-run insight Detailed GuardReport with step-by-step audit

docs.title: 30-Second Example (LangGraph)
docs.text:
LongGuard wraps your agent nodes in a single line of code:

from langgraph.graph import StateGraph
from longguard.integrations.langgraph import add_guard_to_graph
from longguard import GuardConfig

# 1. Build your StateGraph as usual
workflow = StateGraph(AgentState)
workflow.add_node("agent", call_model)
workflow.add_node("tools", tool_node)
workflow.add_edge("agent", "tools")
...

# 2. Add LongGuard — one line!
workflow = add_guard_to_graph(workflow, GuardConfig())
app = workflow.compile()

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:

  • Excluded LangGraph tool nodes cannot dispatch after a trip.
  • Supported CrewAI synchronous ReAct executions receive recovery advice before the next model request, preserve callbacks, count complete actions once and use execution-scoped hooks.

docs.title: Quick Start Guide
docs.text: This guide walks you through installing and using LongGuard in under two minutes.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
LongGuard is available on PyPI with optional dependency extras:

# Core package (zero heavy dependencies — works standalone)
pip install longguard

# With LangGraph support (LangGraph 1.0+)
pip install "longguard[langgraph]"

# With LangChain support
pip install "longguard[langchain]"

# With high-quality sentence embeddings (optional)
pip install "longguard[embeddings]"

# Everything included
pip install "longguard[all]"

Using uv:

uv add longguard

docs.title: 1. LangGraph Integration (1 Line)
docs.text:
Compatible with LangGraph 1.0+ and modern multimodal models (Claude 3.5, GPT-4o, Gemini 1.5/2.0):

from langgraph.graph import StateGraph
from longguard.integrations.langgraph import add_guard_to_graph
from longguard import GuardConfig

# Define your workflow
workflow = StateGraph(AgentState)
workflow.add_node("agent", agent_fn)
workflow.add_node("tools", tool_fn)
workflow.add_edge("agent", "tools")
workflow.add_conditional_edges("tools", should_continue)

# Instrument agent nodes in one line:
workflow = add_guard_to_graph(workflow, GuardConfig(
    tool_repeat_threshold=3,    # 3 identical calls triggers reflection
    max_tokens_per_run=50_000,  # Hard cap per query
    max_steps=25,               # Hard step cap
))

app = workflow.compile()

# Access telemetry report after execution:
guard = workflow.__longguard__
print(guard.get_report().summary())

Node Exclusion: By default, add_guard_to_graph automatically instruments only agent reasoning nodes and skips execution-only nodes ("tools", "action", "__start__", "__end__").

docs.title: 2. Standalone / Custom Agent Loop
docs.text:
If you run a custom while loop or framework-agnostic pipeline:

from longguard import CircuitBreaker, GuardConfig, AgentStep

breaker = CircuitBreaker(GuardConfig(
    tool_repeat_threshold=3,
    max_tokens_per_run=30_000,
))

for i, step in enumerate(agent_loop):
    agent_step = AgentStep(
        step_number=i + 1,
        thought=step.thought,
        action=step.tool_name,
        action_input=step.tool_args,
        observation=step.tool_result,
        tokens_used=step.tokens,
    )

    decision = breaker.check(agent_step)

    if decision.action == "continue":
        pass  # Proceed normally
    elif decision.action == "reflect":
        # Inject recovery prompt into context
        agent_context.append({"role": "system", "content": decision.inject_prompt})
    elif decision.action == "kill":
        print(f"Breaker opened! Reason: {decision.reason}")
        break

# View run summary
print(breaker.report.summary())

docs.title: 3. LangChain Integration
docs.text:
Wrap standard LangChain AgentExecutor:

from langchain.agents import AgentExecutor
from longguard.integrations.langchain import GuardedAgentExecutor, GuardTerminatedException
from longguard import GuardConfig

executor = AgentExecutor.from_agent_and_tools(agent=agent, tools=tools)
guarded = GuardedAgentExecutor(executor, GuardConfig())

try:
    result = guarded.run("Find information about quarterly revenue")
except GuardTerminatedException as exc:
    print(f"Terminated safely: {exc.reason}")
    print(exc.report.summary())

docs.title: Loop Detectors
docs.text: LongGuard includes four battle-tested detectors that analyze different dimensions of an agent's execution.

docs.title: 1. ToolRepeatDetector
docs.text:
What it catches: The agent calls the exact same tool with the exact same arguments repeatedly.

How it works: - Calculates an MD5 fingerprint of (tool_name, serialized_args). - Tracks fingerprints across a sliding window of recent steps. - Smart Polling Awareness: Legitimate polling (e.g. calling check_status(id=123) with changing responses, or calling search(query="different")) is not flagged.

from longguard import ToolRepeatDetector

detector = ToolRepeatDetector(
    repeat_threshold=3,  # 3 identical calls triggers detection
    window=6,            # Look back over the last 6 steps
)

docs.title: 2. SemanticOscillationDetector
docs.text:
What it catches: The agent's chain-of-thought text cycles through the same semantic territory — varying its words slightly, but re-hashing the same thought loop.

How it works: - Computes an embedding for each thought step. - Calculates variance across recent embeddings in a sliding window. Low variance indicates cognitive deadlock. - Embedders: Uses a fast, deterministic, zero-dependency HashBasedEmbedder by default. Optionally upgrade to SentenceTransformerEmbedder via pip install "longguard[embeddings]".

from longguard import SemanticOscillationDetector, HashBasedEmbedder

detector = SemanticOscillationDetector(
    window=8,
    variance_threshold=0.15,
    embedder=HashBasedEmbedder(dimension=64),
)

docs.title: 3. DeadEndDriftDetector
docs.text:
What it catches: The agent is taking actions, but making zero meaningful progress toward the objective.

How it works: Measures three novelty signals on each step: 1. Observation Novelty: Jaccard or cosine similarity of new tool observations vs. prior observations. 2. Action Diversity: Switching to an alternative tool indicates exploration. 3. Thought Novelty: Introduction of new concepts in reasoning.

If none of these novelty signals appear for dead_end_threshold consecutive steps, the detector flags dead-end drift.

from longguard import DeadEndDriftDetector

detector = DeadEndDriftDetector(
    dead_end_threshold=5,
    progress_threshold=0.6,
)

docs.title: 4. TokenVelocityDetector
docs.text:
What it catches: Sudden exponential cost spikes in the agent's thoughts or context.

How it works: - Establishes a baseline of tokens-per-step using an exponential moving average (EMA). - After a short warmup period, if current step velocity exceeds the baseline by velocity_multiplier (e.g. 3.0×), it trips detection.

from longguard import TokenVelocityDetector

detector = TokenVelocityDetector(
    velocity_multiplier=3.0,
    window=5,
    warmup=3,
)

docs.title: How It Works: Circuit Breaker State Machine
docs.text: LongGuard borrows the classic Circuit Breaker pattern from distributed systems (like Netflix Hystrix) and reimagines it for LLM cognitive reasoning.

docs.title: The 4-State Automaton
docs.text: On every step of an agent's run, LongGuard checks all registered loop detectors and navigates a state machine:

docs.title: 1. CLOSED (Normal Operation)
docs.text:
• The agent is executing without detected loops or abnormal token spikes.
  • Detectors run sequentially. Benchmark timings identify the tested backend and workload; model, tool and application latency are separate.
  • Every check returns BreakerDecision(action="continue").

docs.title: 2. REFLECTING (First Loop Detected)
docs.text:
• A detector has identified a loop pattern with high confidence (e.g. 3 identical searches in a row).
  • Instead of terminating the agent, LongGuard injects a Reflect & Pivot system prompt into the agent context.
  • Returns BreakerDecision(action="reflect", inject_prompt="...").

docs.title: 3. HALF_OPEN (The Recovery Window)
docs.text:
• The agent has been prompted to pivot.
  • LongGuard monitors the next step:
  • Success: If the agent switches strategies or makes meaningful progress, the breaker resets back to CLOSED.
  • Failure: If the agent ignores the prompt and repeats the bad pattern, the breaker trips to OPEN.

docs.title: 4. OPEN (Graceful Termination)
docs.text:
• The agent was unable to recover.
  • LongGuard kills the agent cleanly:
  • Saves the entire message history and conversation state.
  • Appends an explanatory AI message to the state so the user isn't left with a broken error.
  • Finalizes the GuardReport with exact timestamps, steps, and kill reasons.

docs.title: Hard Caps
docs.text: In addition to loop detection, LongGuard enforces hard safety caps that bypass the state machine: - Token Budget (max_tokens_per_run): Trips immediately if total query tokens exceed the threshold (e.g. 50,000 tokens). - Step Limit (max_steps): Trips immediately if total reasoning steps exceed the threshold (e.g. 25 steps).

docs.title: Reflect & Pivot Recovery
docs.text:
When a loop is detected, simply killing the agent is a wasted opportunity. In many cases, the LLM simply needs an explicit signal that its current strategy is failing.

LongGuard’s Reflect & Pivot mechanism injects targeted guidance into the agent context to force a course correction.

docs.title: Default Pivot Templates
docs.text:
LongGuard formats a context-aware prompt depending on which detector triggered:

Trigger Pattern Prompt Strategy tool_repeat "You have called {tool} multiple times without success. STOP calling this tool. Try a completely different tool, re-scope your goal, or summarize what you have so far." semantic_oscillation "Your reasoning is cycling between states. Step back, state what you know with certainty, identify the single missing piece of information, and change direction." dead_end_drift "Your last {steps} actions produced no new information. Provide your best answer with current info or abandon this path entirely." token_velocity "Your token consumption has spiked dramatically. Summarize concisely in 2-3 sentences and proceed directly to completion."

docs.title: Customizing Pivot Templates
docs.text:
You can override templates globally or per detector:

from longguard import GuardConfig

config = GuardConfig(
    pivot_templates={
        "tool_repeat": (
            "[SYSTEM ALERT] You have repeated {tool} {count} times! "
            "Explain your difficulty to the user instead of trying again."
        )
    }
)

docs.title: Available Template Variables
docs.text:
• {tool}: Name of the repeating tool.
  • {count}: Number of repetitions.
  • {window}: Sliding window size.
  • {steps}: Consecutive dead-end steps.
  • {velocity} / {baseline}: Token consumption metrics.

docs.title: Reproducible detector evaluation
docs.text: The benchmark uses actual detector implementations and actual circuit decisions. It makes no provider calls, uploads or simulated similarity-score substitutions. Results are provisional because human label review is pending.

docs.title: Reproduce
docs.text:
From the repository root, install development dependencies and run:

uv sync --extra dev
uv run --no-sync python tests/benchmarks/run.py --output tests/benchmarks/results/current-hash.json

The runner explicitly selects hash embeddings for semantic oscillation and Jaccard for dead-end drift. An installed optional backend does not silently change this evaluation. For sentence-transformers, supply a local model snapshot and its pinned revision:

uv run --no-sync python tests/benchmarks/run.py --backend sentence-transformers   --model-path /path/to/local/snapshot --model-revision COMMIT_SHA   --output /tmp/longguard-semantic-results.json

No sentence-transformers model run is claimed in the preview evidence. Hash/Jaccard results cannot establish transformer-backend quality.

docs.title: Corpus and assessment
docs.text:
tests/benchmarks/corpus.json contains 40 original synthetic traces under the repository MIT license: two calibration and eight held-out evaluation traces per detector. Each evaluation group has four loop labels and four healthy labels. The corpus and labels were written before evaluation; related named families cannot cross splits. Traces remain small and correlated, so these counts are not production incident rates or independent statistical samples. The implementation author also authored the labels; a second human must review intent, timing and split separation using tests/benchmarks/LABEL_REVIEW.md.

The assessment unit is one trace for its assigned detector. A positive is timely if first detection is on or before its timely_by step. Calibration is excluded, not silently used to tune defaults. The runner records TP/FP/TN/FN, precision, recall, false-positive rate, denominators, errors, skips, first detection and every circuit outcome. Undefined ratios are JSON null. Circuit evaluation runs all detectors independently of each trace's target label; raw detector accuracy and recovery success are different measurements.

docs.title: Observed hash/Jaccard results
docs.text:
These counts match the unchanged release-baseline detectors and preview detectors.

Detector TP FP TN FN Precision Recall False-positive rate Tool repeat 4 1 3 0 0.80 1.00 0.25 Semantic oscillation 4 2 2 0 0.67 1.00 0.50 Dead-end drift 3 1 3 1 0.75 0.75 0.25 Token velocity 4 1 3 0 0.80 1.00 0.25

Legitimate polling can trigger repetition/dead-end rules, similar useful text can trigger semantic oscillation, and justified large output can trigger token velocity. Switching unproductive actions can hide a dead end. These are exposed limitations, not reasons to silently remove negative traces or tune defaults on the evaluation split.

tests/benchmarks/results/baseline-hash.json evaluates source exported from release commit 7b02104b47277cb5948c84e9ca4830e5f27df8c4; current-hash.json evaluates the edited preview. Each stores source and corpus hashes, command, environment, thresholds, backend, errors and per-trace outcomes. Working-tree flags describe the execution checkout; source paths and hashes identify the actually imported package. Package installation metadata can differ from exported baseline source; source_version records the imported version.

Latency records separate backend initialization, breaker construction, standalone embedding and complete warmed guard.check calls. They exclude model/network/tool execution. An extra embedding probe warms the same texts before guard checks; this is explicitly a warm workload, not first-call end-to-end latency. Timings depend on the local machine. They do not establish application latency, saved tokens, saved dollars or production adoption.

docs.title: Release decision
docs.text:
Maintainers must approve labels, review weak classes and decide whether quality is acceptable before release. The roadmap supplies no fixed accuracy threshold. Keep the original results, record the reviewer and any dataset revision, then evaluate again without relabeling to match scores. Candidate feedback must include useful polling/retries/progress and real failure cases.

Static corpus replay records 21 circuit stops and no clean recovery-after-advice outcomes in the measured hash run. It does not respond to injected prompts. Delivered advice and successful recovery are demonstrated separately by real-framework local tests and examples.

docs.title: Tested execution and compatibility
docs.text: The 0.2.0.dev0 preview extends the existing circuit breaker. Package dependency minimums remain unchanged; they do not guarantee that every permitted framework release supports these execution contracts. Bare import longguard keeps framework dependencies optional.

docs.title: Execution modes
docs.text:
Interface Supported behavior Boundary or unsupported mode CircuitBreaker.check Existing synchronous policy and additive explicit resume Application owns model/tool dispatch and checkpoint integrity guarded, provider converters, GuardedAgentExecutor Existing contracts retained and regression tested Decorator advice must be consumed by the application add_guard_to_graph Existing wrapping; excluded tools are gated after OPEN One mutable guard; reset for a new run; use controlled runner for thread isolation/resume compile_guarded_graph Synchronous START -> agent -> tools/END, tools -> agent; saved node boundaries Exactly two nodes; no async, streaming, subgraphs, parallel nodes, namespaces or checkpoint branching GuardedGraph.resume Same controller/process; matching stopped checkpoint; explicit correction and finite reflection grant Hard caps, completed/failed runs, unknown threads, concurrent continuation and changed checkpoints rejected add_guard_to_crew Sequential, synchronous ReAct Crew.kickoff; public CrewAgentExecutor; separate report per kickoff Async/batch/streaming/hierarchical/native tool batches, delegation, reasoning, planning, memory and CrewAI checkpoint continuation rejected Callback-only CrewGuard Existing callback API, reports and last_reflection No automatic advice delivery or full execution guarantee; attach through add_guard_to_crew for tested recovery Provider cleanup helper Valid OpenAI/Anthropic dictionaries and LangChain message histories Caller must block dispatch; running tools retain unresolved status; invalid IDs rejected

CrewAI's public CrewAgentExecutor is deprecated in the tested release. Its alternative executor is outside this preview's proven mode. A future compatibility change needs real contract tests before widening support. The adapter installs execution-scoped hooks rather than registering global handlers.

docs.title: Usage and side effects
docs.text:
Guards observe completed requests. A token/step cap trips on > and a known estimated-cost cap on >=, as before. The crossing request has already incurred usage. CrewAI's complete action callback follows its tool result: that turn's tool may already have executed before the decision. Subsequent guarded requests stop after a trip.

Actual model usage is used when available. Graph text estimates and CrewAI missing-usage zero defaults are identified in usage_warnings. Cost retains the approximate half-input, half-output token split; it is not provider billing. Guarded continuation retains previous consumption. Changing the budget or importing a report does not authorize execution.

Callbacks and arbitrary tools remain application code: LongGuard cannot undo their side effects or guarantee exactly-once behavior after an application crash. The supported graph continuation avoids replaying completed tools at its saved boundary in the same process.

Newest NumPy 2.5 typing stubs require Python 3.12 syntax. Framework jobs use strict MyPy with a Python 3.12 target; core jobs use the Python 3.11 target and locked dependencies.

Controlled continuation was verified with LangGraph InMemorySaver; other saver implementations are unverified. Pass an unwrapped graph to the controller. Do not share guarded agents or the same guard between crews. Shared provider usage counters across crews are outside tested accounting.

docs.title: Configuration Guide
docs.text: All LongGuard parameters are configured via GuardConfig.

docs.title: Configuration Reference
docs.text:
from longguard import GuardConfig

config = GuardConfig(
    # --- Tool Repeat Detector ---
    tool_repeat_threshold=3,          # N identical calls triggers detection
    tool_repeat_window=6,             # Look-back window size (steps)

    # --- Semantic Oscillation Detector ---
    semantic_variance_threshold=0.15, # Variance threshold below which thoughts are looping
    semantic_window=8,                # Number of thoughts to analyze

    # --- Dead-End Drift Detector ---
    dead_end_threshold=5,             # Consecutive no-progress steps before flagging
    dead_end_progress_threshold=0.6,  # Jaccard/cosine similarity threshold

    # --- Token Velocity Detector ---
    token_velocity_multiplier=3.0,    # Ratio of current velocity to EMA baseline
    token_velocity_window=5,          # Rolling window size
    token_velocity_warmup=3,          # Warmup steps before baseline is active

    # --- Hard Limits ---
    max_tokens_per_run=50_000,        # Hard token spend cap
    max_steps=30,                     # Hard reasoning step limit

    # --- Recovery Settings ---
    max_reflections=2,                # Number of recovery chances before killing
    pivot_templates={},               # Custom prompt templates

    # --- Observability ---
    log_level="WARNING",
    emit_events=True,

    # --- Dollar Cost Tracking (v0.1.3) ---
    model="gpt-4o",                   # Model identifier for built-in pricing lookup
    max_cost_usd=0.50,                # Hard-kill when estimated spend hits $0.50
    # cost_per_input_token=2.5e-6,   # Override: price per input token (USD)
    # cost_per_output_token=10e-6,   # Override: price per output token (USD)
)

docs.title: Universal @guarded Decorator
docs.text: The @guarded decorator brings LongGuard's circuit breaker protection to any Python function, LLM SDK call, generator, or async workflow with zero framework coupling.

docs.title: Why @guarded?
docs.text:
Not every agent uses LangGraph or LangChain. If you build custom while loops, proprietary micro-agents, or standalone tool execution functions, @guarded wraps your logic in a single line:

  • 🛡️ Prevents Runaway Loops: Automatically tracks thoughts, actions, and observations across repeated function calls.
  • 💵 Enforces Spend Limits: Automatically computes dollar costs and trips on max_cost_usd.
  • ⚡ Zero Framework Dependencies: Works with pure Python, openai, anthropic, custom generators, or async coroutines.
  • 📊 Step Telemetry: Preserves a full GuardReport accessible directly via fn.report.

docs.title: 1. Quick Example: Tool / Agent Step Function
docs.text:
Decorate your step execution function with detection parameters:

from longguard import guarded, CircuitBreakerTrippedError

@guarded(max_cost_usd=0.50, tool_repeat_threshold=3)
def execute_agent_step(thought: str, action: str, action_input: dict, observation: str):
    # Your business logic / tool invocation here
    return run_tool(action, action_input)

# Execute steps in your agent loop
try:
    for thought, tool, args in agent_plan:
        result = execute_agent_step(
            thought=thought,
            action=tool,
            action_input=args,
            observation=last_result,
        )
except CircuitBreakerTrippedError as exc:
    print(f"Agent halted safely: {exc.reason}")
    print(exc.report.summary())

docs.title: 2. Decorating OpenAI / Anthropic SDK Calls
docs.text:
Pass LLM responses directly—LongGuard automatically parses response objects and token counts:

import openai
from longguard import guarded

client = openai.OpenAI()

@guarded(model="gpt-4o", max_cost_usd=1.00)
def call_model(messages: list[dict]):
    return client.chat.completions.create(
        model="gpt-4o",
        messages=messages,
    )

# When called, token usage and dollar cost are automatically accumulated
response = call_model([{"role": "user", "content": "Analyze market data"}])

# Inspect telemetry
print(call_model.report.summary())

docs.title: 3. Graceful Fallbacks (on_kill="return")
docs.text:
If you prefer not to catch exceptions, set on_kill="return" or pass a custom callable:

@guarded(tool_repeat_threshold=3, on_kill="return")
def search_database(query: str):
    return db.query(query)

result = search_database("SELECT * FROM users")
# If tripped, returns a safe fallback message instead of raising:
# "Agent terminated by LongGuard: Tool repeat detected: search_database called 3 times"

You can also provide a custom callable for custom fallback payloads:

def handle_trip(decision, *args, **kwargs):
    return {"error": True, "reason": decision.reason, "status": "circuit_open"}

@guarded(on_kill=handle_trip)
def run_action(*args, **kwargs):
    ...

docs.title: 4. Generator Support (Streaming & Step Loops)
docs.text:
@guarded seamlessly protects Python generators:

from longguard import AgentStep, guarded

@guarded(max_steps=10)
def stream_agent_steps():
    for i in range(100):
        yield AgentStep(
            step_number=i + 1,
            thought=f"Reasoning step {i}",
            action="search" if i % 2 == 0 else "analyze",
            action_input={"query": "financials"},
        )

# Iteration stops automatically when the circuit breaker trips
for step in stream_agent_steps():
    print(f"Step {step.step_number} completed")

docs.title: 5. Async Functions
docs.text:
@guarded supports native Python async def functions:

@guarded(max_cost_usd=0.75, tool_repeat_threshold=3)
async def async_agent_step(thought: str, action: str, action_input: dict):
    result = await async_tool_runner(action, action_input)
    return result

docs.title: Telemetry & State Management
docs.text:
Every decorated function exposes its state:

# Access current report
report = my_function.report

# Access underlying CircuitBreaker instance
breaker = my_function.breaker

# Reset telemetry and state for a fresh execution
my_function.reset()

# Check if a reflection prompt was triggered
if my_function.last_reflection_prompt:
    print("Injected pivot:", my_function.last_reflection_prompt)

Once the circuit is OPEN, further calls stop before executing the wrapped body, using the configured on_kill policy. This also applies to post-observation functions and generators. Calling .reset() starts a fresh report and clears .last_reflection_prompt for synchronous, asynchronous and generator wrappers. Previously saved report references retain the prior run.

docs.title: Framework Coverage & Trust: development evidence
docs.text: Status: Unpublished 0.2.0.dev0 preview on feat/v020-framework-trust. Implementation baseline: 7b02104b47277cb5948c84e9ca4830e5f27df8c4 (v0.1.4). Local verification date: 2026-10-08. Release publication remains a maintainer decision.

docs.title: Starting audit
docs.text:
The nested repository began clean at the exact roadmap release SHA. Package and import versions were 0.1.4. Contribution guidance, source, tests, examples and workflows were inspected; no applicable AGENTS.md was present. The configured origin is the Abdullahbinmushtaq fork. Its tag query returned no tags. Upstream main and v0.1.4 both matched the starting SHA; upstream tags also include v0.1.3 and v0.1.1. Direct PyPI metadata and upstream GitHub release API checks still reported 0.1.4; the latest GitHub release was published 2026-09-24. Upstream open pull-request and issue queries returned empty lists. The development version was unused on PyPI when checked; no tag or package was published.

A source export of the baseline passed 271 tests using Python 3.12 with the required async test plugin. System Python 3.14 without that plugin initially failed an async test; development environments now use the documented dev extra. The release's README fixed count was stale; the README now describes the test command without a frozen count.

Core policy remains in core/breaker.py; config.py owns defaults, core/step.py normalization, core/detectors/ detector interfaces, core/reporter.py telemetry, core/pivot.py recovery prompts, and integrations/ framework execution. Existing guarded, provider conversions, pricing, report persistence, lazy integrations and py.typed are retained.

docs.title: Executed verification
docs.text:
• Baseline Python 3.12 suite: 271 passed.
  • Core-only locked Python 3.10.21: 362 passed, 3 optional/release-script modules skipped; strict MyPy passed. Release tooling runs on Python 3.12.
  • Core-only locked Python 3.11.16: 365 passed, 2 optional framework modules skipped; strict MyPy passed.
  • Clean wheel and sdist installs passed outside the repository; bare imports load no optional framework/provider modules and include py.typed. An actual published 0.1.4 install was upgraded to the local preview wheel and its saved report loaded successfully. Both quickstarts ran outside the source tree using the installed wheel and real framework extras.
  • Combined locked frameworks (LangGraph 1.2.11, LangChain 1.3.18/core 1.6.1, CrewAI 1.15.22): 402 passed, 97.60% statement coverage, strict MyPy passed with the preserved Python 3.10 target.
  • Combined newest frameworks: 402 passed, 97.60% statement coverage (1,915 measured statements; 46 uncovered). Ruff, strict MyPy (Python 3.12 target), strict MkDocs and wheel/sdist build passed. Exact commands/output are recorded in the local release-evidence.json and release-coverage.json generated by scripts/verify_release.py. Framework CI and release checks enforce at least 95% aggregate statement coverage; optional dependencies are required for these checks.
  • Real graph fixtures check normal completion, delivered recovery, trips, original-ID cleanup, cumulative resume, counted effects, independent threads, concurrent resume, changed checkpoints and the legacy dispatch path. Provider cleanup is parsed by the real LangChain message converter for OpenAI and Anthropic histories, including an existing failed result. Real CrewAI fixtures check normal/recovered/stopped executions, callbacks, fresh reports, caps, reattachment, shared-agent isolation and unsupported-mode rejection.
  • Provider, decorator, pricing, historical reporting, lazy imports and original contracts retain their existing regression tests. A fixture was saved by the installed public v0.1.4 package.
  • Benchmark hash/Jaccard baseline/current counts match; thresholds and algorithms were not tuned. The corpus has 32 held-out traces and zero reported execution errors. Human label review is pending.

The compatible locked and newest framework environments are enumerated in the compatibility matrix. Latest NumPy typing stubs use Python 3.12 syntax, so the framework strict-typing check uses Python 3.12; core strict checks now target Python 3.11 after raising the minimum supported version. Warnings include CrewAI's deprecated public executor and callback serialization. Tests isolate credential-file storage and unrelated event listeners without replacing framework execution. No live provider requests or credentials are needed. The graph example was run directly; the CrewAI example was run with temporary credential storage because the workspace cannot write CrewAI's normal home storage location.

docs.title: Coverage follow-up
docs.text:
Coverage increased from 89% / 306 tests to 97.60% / 402 tests without excluding production code. The 96 additional cases exercise public exports, configuration validation, decorator extraction and termination policies, framework normalization, checkpoint rejection, CrewAI unsupported modes and concurrent execution, and custom-detector failure isolation.

These tests exposed two decorator defects. Once the circuit is OPEN, synchronous, asynchronous and generator wrappers now stop before further body execution, including post-observation functions. Async and generator resets now expose the new report and clear old reflection advice. Regression tests assert side-effect counts, original reports and all kill policies.

Coverage measures executed statements, not complete branch coverage or detector accuracy. Optional embedding-model execution, live provider acceptance and release approval remain separate validation work.

docs.title: Maintainer delivery and feedback
docs.text:
Engineering work is local and reviewable. No GitHub PR was opened: no GitHub CLI or connector is available and no GitHub API credential is present. The local draft description is .github/PR_v0.2.0_DRAFT.md; maintainers can split review into core/protocol, framework, and benchmark/release changes. No main push, merge, stable tag or publication was performed.

Before promoting this preview to an RC or stable version:

  1. Review labels/split leakage in tests/benchmarks/LABEL_REVIEW.md, then rerun the evaluation and record the quality decision, especially legitimate polling and semantic false positives.
  2. Execute hosted CI, including macOS; local Linux results do not prove that matrix.
  3. Review supported framework mode restrictions and deprecated CrewAI executor behavior.
  4. Choose an unused RC version, update package/import/lockfile/changelog together, verify the exact source tag and built wheel/sdist, and perform candidate clean-install/upgrade checks.
  5. Maintainer publishes the candidate through the project's chosen PyPI credentials/procedure (no existing automated PyPI workflow was found), then checks published metadata and fresh installs.
  6. Collect minimized/redacted reports from candidate users: successful useful work, false positives, recovery failures, replay concerns and framework versions. Record evidence and priority; defer unrelated feature requests. No candidate/community feedback is claimed here.
  7. Confirm acceptance and promote only after maintainer approval. The stable version must be unused and the final artifacts rebuilt from the reviewed source.

Sentence-transformers quality, live provider acceptance, community feedback, hosted CI and human label review remain explicit gaps. Reports are local telemetry, not cross-process execution checkpoints or billing statements.

docs.text:

#   "kill_reason": "reflection_failed: tool_repeat...",
#   "detections": [...],
#   "step_timeline": [...]
# }

docs.title: Saving & Loading Reports (v0.1.3)
docs.text:
Persist run telemetry to disk for CI artifacts, post-mortem debugging, or dashboards:

# Save to JSON (zero extra dependencies)
report.save("run_report.json")

# Save to YAML (requires: pip install pyyaml)
report.save("run_report.yaml")

# Load a saved report back for analysis
from longguard import GuardReport
loaded = GuardReport.load("run_report.json")
print(loaded.summary())

docs.title: Event Callbacks
docs.text:
Stream events to LangSmith, Datadog, or custom webhooks:

def on_guard_event(event_name: str, payload: dict):
    print(f"LongGuard Event [{event_name}]: {payload}")

breaker = CircuitBreaker(
    config=GuardConfig(emit_events=True),
    event_callback=on_guard_event,
)

# Emits:
# - "detection": loop pattern detected
# - "reflect": pivot prompt injected
# - "kill": agent killed
# - "recovered": circuit recovered to CLOSED

docs.title: Development-preview metadata
docs.text:
Reports add run_id, continuations, tool_dispositions, and usage_warnings. Older saved reports still load with defaults for missing fields; existing field names and estimated-cost semantics remain. New metadata records explicit correction/granted allowance, original tool call IDs and skipped/running status, and missing/estimated usage. It contains no executable checkpoint and does not authorize continuation. Loading a report is inspection only.

Reports can contain application messages and corrections. Keep them local and redact sensitive text before submitting a minimized reproduction. This release adds no automatic uploads.

docs.title: CrewAI integration
docs.text:
Use the existing add_guard_to_crew API for the tested sequential synchronous ReAct mode. It preserves prior agent and crew callbacks, injects Reflect & Pivot into the next model context, and raises GuardTerminatedException on unrecoverable loops or hard caps.

from crewai.agents.crew_agent_executor import CrewAgentExecutor
from longguard import GuardConfig
from longguard.integrations.crewai import add_guard_to_crew, GuardTerminatedException

# Configure your Agent with executor_class=CrewAgentExecutor, allow_delegation=False,
# a ReAct LLM (supports_function_calling() is False), and synchronous tasks.
crew = add_guard_to_crew(crew, GuardConfig(tool_repeat_threshold=3, max_steps=30))
try:
    result = crew.kickoff()
except GuardTerminatedException as exc:
    print(exc.reason)
    exc.report.save("stopped-crew.json")

See tested compatibility before adapting an existing crew. The declared dependency minimum is broader than the execution-hook versions tested. Missing public scoped-hook APIs produce a clear error. Async, native tool batches, streaming, hierarchical processing, checkpoint continuation and additional model paths are unsupported. The deprecated public CrewAgentExecutor is selected explicitly; no private executor methods are replaced. LongGuard wraps the public kickoff entry point and scopes its hooks to execution.

Every kickoff starts a fresh report and budget. Concurrent kickoff of the same guarded crew is rejected. Reattaching the same guard is idempotent; changing an attached configuration requires a new crew. Execution callbacks receive their normal events. ToolResult and the complete AgentAction can both arrive for a tool turn; the action is accounted once.

CrewAI can suppress identical tool execution itself. Repeated model tool requests are still observed. Missing usage appears in usage_warnings; cost is estimated, not billed spend. A tool in the current turn may finish before its action callback trips the circuit.

Callback-only CrewGuard.step_callback remains available. It exposes last_reflection but cannot automatically deliver it or govern every execution path. Use full attachment for the tested advice/termination contract.

The credential-free examples/crewai_guarded.py runs actual CrewAI with a deterministic local model and tool. No provider SDK calls, secrets or paid requests are required. Tests isolate only CrewAI credential-file storage and unrelated event listeners; execution remains real.

docs.title: LangChain Integration
docs.text: LongGuard integrates with LangChain via the GuardedAgentExecutor middleware.

docs.title: AgentExecutor Middleware
docs.text:
Wrap any standard LangChain AgentExecutor:

from langchain.agents import AgentExecutor
from longguard.integrations.langchain import GuardedAgentExecutor, GuardTerminatedException
from longguard import GuardConfig

# 1. Create your standard executor
agent_executor = AgentExecutor.from_agent_and_tools(
    agent=agent,
    tools=tools,
    verbose=True,
)

# 2. Wrap with LongGuard
guarded = GuardedAgentExecutor(agent_executor, GuardConfig(
    max_tokens_per_run=40_000,
    max_steps=20,
))

# 3. Run safely
try:
    result = guarded.run("Summarize the quarterly financial report")
    print(result)
except GuardTerminatedException as exc:
    print(f"Agent terminated by LongGuard: {exc.reason}")
    print(exc.report.summary())

docs.title: Manual Step Checking
docs.text:
If you are implementing a custom agent loop rather than AgentExecutor:

decision = guarded.check_step(action=agent_action, observation=tool_output)

if decision.action == "kill":
    raise GuardTerminatedException(decision.reason, decision.report)

docs.title: LangGraph Integration
docs.text: LongGuard provides seamless, non-invasive integration for LangGraph 1.0+.

docs.title: 1-Line StateGraph Wrapping
docs.text:
The easiest way to guard your LangGraph workflow is add_guard_to_graph():

from langgraph.graph import StateGraph, START, END
from longguard.integrations.langgraph import add_guard_to_graph
from longguard import GuardConfig

# 1. Build your StateGraph as usual
workflow = StateGraph(AgentState)
workflow.add_node("agent", agent_node)
workflow.add_node("tools", tool_node)
workflow.add_edge(START, "agent")
workflow.add_conditional_edges("agent", should_continue, ["tools", END])
workflow.add_edge("tools", "agent")

# 2. Add LongGuard in one line
workflow = add_guard_to_graph(workflow, GuardConfig(
    tool_repeat_threshold=3,
    max_tokens_per_run=50_000,
    max_steps=25,
))

app = workflow.compile()

docs.title: What Happens When Terminated?
docs.text:
When the circuit breaker opens and kills the agent: 1. LongGuard preserves the full messages history. 2. It appends an explanation message to messages: 

[LongGuard] Agent terminated: reflection_failed: tool_repeat (confidence: 100%).
The agent was stuck in a reasoning loop and could not recover after reflection attempts.
3. It sets __longguard_terminated__ = True and __longguard_reason__ = "..." on the state dictionary. 4. Your should_continue conditional edge can safely terminate to END without unhandled crashes:

def should_continue(state: AgentState):
    if state.get("__longguard_terminated__"):
        return END
    if not state["messages"][-1].tool_calls:
        return END
    return "tools"

docs.title: Excluding Execution Nodes
docs.text:
By default, add_guard_to_graph ignores execution-only nodes ("tools", "action", "__start__", "__end__"). You can customize this list:

workflow = add_guard_to_graph(
    workflow,
    GuardConfig(),
    exclude_nodes=["tools", "my_custom_db_writer"],
)

docs.title: Accessing Telemetry
docs.text:
After execution, the guard report is stored on the graph instance:

guard = workflow.__longguard__
print(guard.get_report().summary())

docs.title: Explicit checkpoint continuation (development preview)
docs.text:
For isolated runs and safe explicit continuation, use the additive controller:

from langgraph.checkpoint.memory import InMemorySaver
from longguard import GuardConfig, compile_guarded_graph

# graph must have START -> agent -> tools/END and tools -> agent.
runner = compile_guarded_graph(graph, GuardConfig(max_steps=30), checkpointer=InMemorySaver())
config = {"configurable": {"thread_id": "job-1"}}
result = runner.invoke({"messages": messages}, config)
if result.get("__longguard_terminated__"):
    print(runner.get_report("job-1").kill_reason)
    # Human/application must explicitly choose correction; a hard-cap stop is ineligible.
    result = runner.resume(config, correction="Use the existing results and finish",
                           additional_reflections=1)

The controller stops at persisted node boundaries before dispatching a killed turn's tools. Original-ID pending calls receive truthful skipped/error results; completed results remain. Advice is delivered after pending tool results and before the next agent. Run a copyable stop/resume example with python examples/langgraph_resume.py after installing the graph extra.

Only detector-recovery failures with budget remaining can resume. A nonempty correction and positive finite reflection grant are required. Tokens, steps, estimated cost, detections and reflection count remain cumulative. A changed checkpoint, implicit reinvocation, unknown run, completed run or concurrent continuation is rejected. A different thread_id starts a new run with an independent report. A loaded report or checkpoint alone cannot reconstruct the live guard in a different process.

Support is synchronous, one agent node plus one tool node. Async, streaming, parallel graph nodes, subgraphs, branching and namespaces are outside the tested contract. See tested compatibility. Completed tools are not replayed by the supported resume path; arbitrary application crashes and external side effects still require application idempotency.

The existing add_guard_to_graph retains its API. Excluded tool/action nodes now raise CircuitBreakerTrippedError if routing attempts to dispatch them after termination. Reusing that legacy graph shares one mutable guard; explicitly reset for a new run. Use the controlled runner for independent thread accounting.

docs.title: Raw Client Integration (OpenAI & Anthropic)
docs.text: Use LongGuard directly with the OpenAI or Anthropic Python SDK — no LangGraph or LangChain required.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
LongGuard v0.1.3 adds two class methods to AgentStep that extract all necessary information from a raw SDK response using duck-typing (no hard SDK dependency):

AgentStep.from_openai_response(response, step_number, *, observation=None, latency_ms=0.0)
AgentStep.from_anthropic_response(response, step_number, *, observation=None, latency_ms=0.0)

Both methods extract:

Field OpenAI Anthropic thought choices[0].message.content All text content blocks joined action tool_calls[0].function.name First tool_use block name action_input Parsed JSON from tool_calls[0].function.arguments tool_use block input dict tokens_used usage.total_tokens usage.input_tokens + output_tokens

docs.title: OpenAI Example
docs.text:
import openai
from longguard import AgentStep, CircuitBreaker, GuardConfig

client = openai.OpenAI()
breaker = CircuitBreaker(GuardConfig(
    model="gpt-4o",       # enables dollar-cost tracking
    max_cost_usd=0.50,    # hard-kill if run exceeds $0.50
    max_steps=30,
))

messages = [{"role": "user", "content": "Research and summarize AI trends in 2025."}]
observation = None

for i in range(1, 31):
    response = client.chat.completions.create(
        model="gpt-4o",
        messages=messages,
        tools=[...],  # your tool definitions
    )

    # One-line conversion
    step = AgentStep.from_openai_response(
        response,
        step_number=i,
        observation=observation,
    )

    decision = breaker.check(step)

    if decision.action == "kill":
        print(f"⛔ Halted: {decision.reason}")
        break
    elif decision.action == "reflect":
        messages.append({"role": "system", "content": decision.inject_prompt})

    if step.action is None:
        break  # agent gave final answer

    # Run the tool and get the observation for next step
    observation = your_tool_runner(step.action, step.action_input)
    messages.append({"role": "tool", "content": observation})

print(breaker.report.summary())
# → Estimated Cost: $0.0143 USD (gpt-4o)

docs.title: Supported Models & Pricing
docs.text:
LongGuard's built-in pricing table was verified against official provider sources on 2026-10-09. It uses standard, uncached text-token prices at the base context tier. See the pricing sources and availability audit for supported providers, removals, retirement dates, and promotional price expiry dates.

The selected registry excludes GPT-4/Turbo, GPT-3.5 Turbo, the o-series, Gemini 2.5, Command R+, and the March 2024 Command R releases. Use list_supported_models() to check whether a model has a built-in price.

Long-context premiums, caching, batch/priority rates, multimodal usage, and tool fees require user-supplied prices or separate accounting. Removed model IDs return None; provide explicit rates when estimating historical usage or enterprise contracts.

from longguard import list_supported_models, compute_cost

# List all models with known pricing
print(list_supported_models())
# Includes 'claude-sonnet-5-5', 'gemini-3.8-flash', 'gpt-6.1-sol', ...

# Compute cost for a specific workload
cost = compute_cost("gpt-4o", input_tokens=10_000, output_tokens=3_000)
# $0.055

docs.title: Pricing Resolution Order
docs.text:
1. User-supplied — cost_per_input_token + cost_per_output_token in GuardConfig
  2. Built-in table — automatic lookup by model name (case-insensitive)
  3. Graceful fallback — estimated_cost_usd = None if model not recognised; max_cost_usd cap silently skipped

For models not yet in the table, supply your own prices:

config = GuardConfig(
    cost_per_input_token=3e-6,   # look up from provider pricing page
    cost_per_output_token=15e-6,
    max_cost_usd=1.00,
)

docs.title: Runnable Example
docs.text:
A complete self-contained demo (runs without an API key via mock):

python examples/openai_raw_guard.py

docs.title: Stop with pending tool calls
docs.text:
Converters preserve their existing first-action summary. Cleanup must inspect the original provider conversation to preserve every tool call identifier:

from longguard.integrations.messages import resolve_pending_tool_calls

# First stop dispatching new tools. Append the actual assistant response to messages.
cleanup = resolve_pending_tool_calls(messages, decision.reason, protocol="openai")
messages = cleanup.messages
# Append cleanup.dispositions to your report if desired.

Use protocol="anthropic" for Anthropic tool-use blocks. Completed results remain unchanged; unstarted calls receive failed/skipped results and never a fabricated success. If calls are already running, pass running_ids={...}: they remain unresolved until real completion. Do not continue the provider conversation with unresolved running calls. The helper itself never cancels or executes tools, and assumes a valid conversation prefix.
